# Fixtures that must never be auto-run by a pull request's scoped conformance.
#
# ci.yml scopes a PR's conformance to the fixtures the PR touched. Some fixtures
# cannot pass in CI no matter what the PR changed - the blocker is the test
# environment or the job's time budget, not the diff - so running them turns
# every PR that touches them red and bills Azure for the privilege. They are
# listed here and subtracted from the PR scope, with the reason on each.
#
# Same format as conformance-matrix.txt: one fixture per line, '#' comments and
# blank lines ignored. A name may NOT appear in both files - conformance-scope.sh
# fails the run if one does, so the two cannot drift into disagreement.
#
# This file does NOT affect push-to-main or nightly. Those are driven purely by
# conformance-matrix.txt; a fixture absent from that file already does not run.
#
# Removing a line here is how a fixture becomes PR-eligible again - do it once
# the blocker below is gone.

# --- Blocked by the CI environment: no diff can make these pass -------------

# Needs a real owned domain (Azure serves an ownership challenge the CI
# subscription cannot answer).
custom-hostname-binding

# Azure validates an App Service certificate against a verified custom domain on
# the referenced plan; with no verified domain, no certificate is accepted.
app-service-certificate

# --- Exceed the conformance-tests job's timeout-minutes: 120 ----------------
# Measured lifecycles: vpn-gateway ~60 min, the two virtual-network-gateway
# fixtures ~60-90 min, and a lifecycle runs create + update + destroy +
# recreate + OOB-delete. scripts/ci/run-conformance-phase.sh already carries
# their per-command budgets, so raising the job cap is the only change needed to
# make them runnable.
vpn-gateway
virtual-network-gateway
virtual-network-gateway-connection
